## TL;DR

The review correctly identified that the initial QA note did not establish create, screenshot, or dependency behavior. I addressed the dependency UI gap by adding a searchable multi-select prerequisite picker to Manual task creation and task Details, wiring it to the existing API fields, and adding focused tests. I then drove the real UI headlessly at 1280 and 375 pixels against `just serve-noauth` from a detached scratch worktree. Since that server intentionally rejects writes, Playwright intercepted only the three write requests and supplied success responses; this verified the UI payloads and transitions. Existing tests exercised the backend create, screenshot storage, and dependency persistence paths. The updated QA note explains this evidence and its boundary.

## Work and rationale

The initial browser pass showed that the creation panel and task drawer rendered, but it did not verify the flows named by the task. The automated review was right to reject that as incomplete. I re-read the round-one report and traced the earlier Create result to the preview-child guard in the router. `just serve-noauth` starts with `REPOOS_PREVIEW_CHILD=1`; the guard correctly blocks non-GET/HEAD requests. I did not weaken or bypass that guard.

While tracing the dependency path, I found that the backend already supported `dependsOn` on create and PATCH and validated IDs, self-dependencies, and cycles. The UI had no way to set a prerequisite: the task Details view only displayed existing dependency rows, and the new-task payload omitted the field. I added `TaskDependencyPicker.vue`, a search-and-select control that excludes the current task, shows a bounded set of matches, and lets users remove selected prerequisites. Manual task creation includes the picker, and the task Details editor includes it alongside the existing editable fields. The form sends `dependsOn` through the server’s existing create and PATCH contracts. The new-task store initializes and resets the field so a prior selection cannot leak into a later task.

The UI tests cover filtering, current-task exclusion, selection and removal. TaskDrawer-level tests select a prerequisite in Manual creation and in Details, then assert the exact `dependsOn` values sent in POST and PATCH bodies. Existing attachment tests verify screenshot file storage and retrieval. Existing create route tests verify that task creation writes through the server path. Core dependency tests verify serialization, persistence, and validation. I ran those focused suites and the changed UI build.

The second review found no additional code bugs, but its verification evidence was incomplete because the automatic handoff captures had not run after the earlier check stopped. I also reran the changed-path gate and found the picker’s 10 px task-status label below the contrast floor in Solarized Dark. I changed all small status, empty-state, and selected-dependency text in this component to use the foreground token, covering the same low-contrast pattern across the picker. I retained the declared captures for both create and edit states so RepoOS can capture them from the reviewed tree during handoff.

For the browser pass, I built the UI in a detached scratch worktree and started the required auth-less server with `just serve-noauth 7272`. Playwright Chromium stayed headless. GETs came from the server; Playwright intercepted only POST/PATCH mutation requests because the server intentionally rejects writes. The create flow selected a dependency and a PNG, observed a POST body containing `dependsOn: ["1169"]`, then observed the screenshot attachment request for the created task. A successful mocked response closed the form. The Details flow selected prerequisite #1169 and observed a PATCH body containing the same dependency ID; a successful response cleared the unsaved-changes panel. At both 1280 and 375 widths, the creation and Details pickers were visible and the document had no horizontal overflow.

## Approaches tried

I first followed the task’s exact server setup and saw HTTP 405 on Create. I instrumented the network request and confirmed the UI displayed `preview servers are read-only`, which led to the router guard rather than an app defect. I inspected `repoos serve --preview-overrides` as a possible writable alternative, but the CLI correctly rejected direct server launch from this managed agent process. I therefore kept the server read-only and used Playwright interception only for UI success-path coverage. I paired that browser evidence with existing backend tests instead of claiming the mocked response persisted data.

## Challenges and blockers

The required auth-less preview server cannot perform real writes, by design, and direct writable server startup is blocked in this managed session. Consequently, successful create, upload, and update persistence were not established by this browser session itself. The server-side tests do exercise their storage and write helpers in disposable temporary repositories, while the browser tests prove that the UI submits the expected fields and handles success responses. I made this distinction explicit in the QA note. The task’s request to commit the docs conflicts with the active-turn instruction not to run `git add` or commit; the QA note remains for RepoOS-managed finalization. I did not modify `repoos.toml`.

## Key learnings

The preview write guard is intentional, and a failed POST there is expected rather than evidence of a broken create path. Future UI QA tasks that need real persistence should use a dedicated writable test harness or pair read-only browser coverage with API-level temporary-repository tests. The dependency API was already present, but the UI had only a read view; the new picker closes that functional gap. Browser route interception is useful for checking request shape and success-state handling, but it must be labeled as mocked evidence and paired with backend persistence tests.
